Subject: Re: Clarification request: multi-path availability reconciliation (May 8–10)

Ben —

Thanks for taking a look. We saw a 22% spike in error-rate and elevated p95 latency for API traffic to the Redwood endpoint over May 8–10 between 03:00–05:00 UTC each day. Our SLOs are sensitive to sustained p95 regressions, and the incidents materially affected a small set of patient-facing features.

We opened an internal ticket and our on-call traced a correlated increase in TCP RSTs coming from an intermediate CDN vendor. Aegis confirmed they had a regional configuration rollout during that window but say it only impacted a small subset of POPs.

We believe this should be treated as a partial degradation window and are requesting the standard uptime credit calculation for partial degradations under §3.2 of the SLA. Please confirm how Redwood apportions time when a third-party CDN is involved and whether those minutes are excluded as a third-party maintenance event.

Attached: a short CSV with our symptom timestamps and sample error logs.

—Samir

Subject: RE: Clarification request: multi-path availability reconciliation (May 8–10)

Ben / Lauren —

I pulled the egress traces and token-acceptance logs for the May 8–10 windows. Summary:

- We observe elevated connect timeouts and a 5xx surge from our edge facing the Aegis POP set in us-west-2 between 03:12–04:55 UTC on those days.
- Our runtime still had accepted sessions routed over alternate paths for ~63% of the affected requests; the remaining 37% experienced increased retries and eventual 5xx.
- There was no scheduled maintenance on Redwood’s control plane or serving pool during that period — nothing in our release calendar or autoscaler logs.

Interpretation and recommended classification:
- This matches a partial degradation by our SLA definitions: service was partially available (some requests succeeded via fallback paths) while other traffic degraded.
- Because the root cause appears to have been intermittent failures in an intermediate CDN layer (Aegis), we need to determine whether Aegis’s rollout qualifies as a third-party maintenance event that the SLA excludes. Per §6.1, third-party vendor outages are excluded only when the vendor declares a maintenance and provides a remediation window AND our routing could not reasonably mitigate.

Proposed credit approach:
- Calculate total affected customer-minute buckets across the window (using NovaHealth traffic share to the affected POPs).
- Apportion credit only for minutes where our token acceptance rate for NovaHealth fell below the partial-degradation threshold and where alternate paths did not restore success.

Attachments: I exported egress traces (redwood-egress-trace-20270510.txt) and a preliminary minute-level tally. I can hand this off to Billing to compute the final credit amount once legal/procurement confirms acceptance criteria.

-Rishi

Subject: Re: Clarification request: multi-path availability reconciliation (May 8–10)

Samir —

Appreciate your patience on this. Quick summary of findings and next steps (we’ve attached the proposed spreadsheet):

What we found
- Root cause: intermittent configuration rollout at Aegis POPs caused elevated TCP RSTs and increased retries for a subset of flows between 03:12–04:55 UTC on May 8, 9, and 10.
- Scope: NovaHealth experienced degraded requests for ~37% of attempts routed to the affected POPs. For the remainder, our smart routing and retransmit behavior recovered traffic.
- Redwood internal state: no control-plane maintenance or autoscaler event; serving pools remained healthy.

How we classify it under the SLA
- Because the primary failure originated in an upstream CDN, this meets the definition of a third-party incident for initial attribution, however:
  - Aegis has not formally declared the rollout as a scheduled maintenance during that window (we asked them; their ops team acknowledged a config push but did not mark it as maintenance).
  - Under §6.1, we can only exclude time as third-party maintenance if the vendor: (a) declares maintenance or (b) provides explicit remediation/rollback that was beyond our control. They did not.

Proposed customer credit (transparent calculation)
- We propose applying the partial-degradation credit for the minutes where NovaHealth’s token acceptance rate fell below the SLA threshold and where our fallback did not fully mitigate. You’ll see the minute-level tally and the resulting credit in the attached XLSX (proposed-credit-calculation.xlsx).

Next steps
- If you accept the proposed calculation, we’ll generate a formal credit note and route it via your procurement contact (please confirm the name).
- If you prefer Redwood to exclude the window because you want vendor-handled remediation, we can re-open for joint attribution with Aegis but that typically delays resolution.

I’ve CC’d Aegis ops to confirm their side; we welcome a short call if you want to walk through the minute-level data.

Thanks again — I’ll stay on this until it’s closed.
